nhSignalTitle: New Hampshire publishes a specific process for toll and court collections
nhSignalSummary: New Hampshire law describes toll notices with transaction-specific details and a defined enforcement path. Judicial Branch materials separately describe judgment collection through filed motions, service, hearings, and court orders.
reusedCaseSignalTitle: The core case number appears in official scam-alert examples
reusedCaseSignalSummary: Official scam alerts published by Dallas and Miami-Dade show the same 26-TR-273196 core case number in fake traffic notices.
nhSafeTitle: Check the toll or case outside this notice
nhSafeSummary: Use New Hampshire’s official toll or court channels before paying through any route printed in this notice.
nhSafeStep1: Check the toll through the official NH E-ZPass site using information you already know.
nhSafeStep2: If the notice claims a court order or judgment, contact the New Hampshire Judicial Branch independently.
nhSafeStep3: Do not use the payment route in the notice until the demand matches an official record.
